title: Sunny Balwani: The Other Theranos Conviction
summary:
Sunny Balwani and the Theranos collapse explained from the court record: why the other Theranos conviction stuck.

Elizabeth Holmes was acquitted of defrauding patients; her former number two, Ramesh 'Sunny' Balwani, was convicted on all twelve counts. An appeals court even agreed a witness at his trial gave 'actually false' testimony, and he still lost; on 5 October 2026 the Supreme Court declined to hear his case. Using the Ninth Circuit's December 2025 amended opinion, the Supreme Court docket, the US Attorney's sentencing release, the federal lab regulator's March 2016 sanctions letter and trial reporting, we follow the lab he oversaw, the patients, the pitch to investors, the two trials and the appeal. SEC claims are allegations; criminal findings are the jury's and the courts'. 'Our analysis' is labelled as our own reading.

scenes.say: Chapter one. The number two. Was Balwani really just Holmes's deputy?
The appeals court says he and Holmes were in a romantic relationship from 2004 to 2016.

visual.text: Holmes and Balwani's relationship, per the court

scenes.say: He joined Theranos in 2009 and was later appointed its president and chief operating officer.
Prosecutors say he worked there from September 2009 to July 2016, as board member, chief operating officer and president.
And he had a stake. Nearly thirty million shares, more than six per cent of the company.
According to the court, he oversaw the patient-testing lab and was the main contact for the retail partners, Safeway and Walgreens.

visual.title: What the court says he ran

scenes.say: The court adds that the exact split of duties between him and Holmes was disputed at trial.

visual.text: The precise division of responsibilities between Holmes and Balwani was disputed at trial.

scenes.say: His own words, shown to his jury, according to Fortune: I am responsible for everything at Theranos.

visual.text: I am responsible for everything at Theranos.
visual.by: Balwani, text to Holmes, as reported by Fortune

scenes.say: Chapter two. The lab. What did the man in charge of it know?
Theranos promised fast blood tests from a few drops, run on its own machine, the Edison.
The court says Theranos developed three hundred small-sample tests. Only twelve were ever run on the Edison.
For visiting investors, the court says, the device ran a null protocol, while some samples were secretly run on other companies' machines.

visual.title: The VIP demo, per the court
items: Some samples went to third-party machines

scenes.say: Former employees testified that the Edison consistently failed quality control checks. The court says they told Holmes and Balwani in real time.

visual.header: Trial evidence, per the Ninth Circuit
visual.title: Inside the lab

scenes.say: In a text to Holmes, reported by NBC Bay Area, Balwani called a Theranos lab a disaster zone.

visual.by: Balwani, text to Holmes, as reported by NBC Bay Area

scenes.say: Associated Press reporting dates that message to 2014.
In late 2015, federal inspectors arrived unannounced. They found deficiencies posing immediate jeopardy to patient health.

visual.label: to patient health, the regulator concluded

scenes.say: Here is the regulator's letter of March 2016. Look who it was addressed to.
It proposed revoking the lab's licence, fines of ten thousand dollars a day, and a ban of at least two years on its owners and operators.
For several deficiencies, Theranos told the regulator no patient impact was expected. The agency said it gave no information on how it reached that conclusion.
Chapter three. The patients. What happens when a blood test is wrong?
Prosecutors laid it out after sentencing. A doctor received repeatedly elevated results on a test used to screen for prostate cancer.

visual.header: US Attorney, Northern District of California
visual.title: Patient 1: PSA test

scenes.say: Conventional tests approved by regulators later showed those results were inaccurate.
Pregnant women received wrong pregnancy-hormone results. One was told she was likely miscarrying. Conventional tests showed a viable pregnancy.

visual.title: Patient 2: pregnancy tests
items: Wrong HCG results for pregnant women
One told she was likely miscarrying
She later delivered a healthy baby

scenes.say: A Theranos employee on blood thinners got results far from earlier tests. A doctor changed the dose. A traditional lab later showed the change wasn't needed.

visual.text: Medication changed on a result later shown unnecessary

scenes.say: The court says evidence linked Balwani to sending out those inaccurate results, and to buying adverts for Theranos wellness centres in Arizona.

visual.title: Linked to Balwani, per the court

scenes.say: In the end, prosecutors say, Theranos itself concluded a patient impact existed for every test run on a patient, and it voided all tests run on its analyser.

visual.label: patient tests on the Edison voided

scenes.say: The trial judge found that decision was not voluntary. The appeals court let that stand, and said at Holmes's trial it could show what she knew.

visual.text: Voiding every Edison result was probative of Holmes's knowledge.

scenes.say: Patient health, the US Attorney said, is the highest priority of our healthcare system. And of Balwani, she said: he chose deceit over candour with patients in need of medical care.

visual.text: He chose deceit over candor with patients in need of medical care.
visual.by: US Attorney Stephanie M. Hinds, 7 Dec 2022

scenes.say: Chapter four. The pitch. Why did so much money keep coming in?
By March 2015, prosecutors say, Theranos had raised more than seven hundred and thirty million dollars in its Series C rounds.

visual.label: raised from Series C-1 and C-2 investors by March 2015

scenes.say: The court says Theranos had no revenue in 2012 or 2013, and lost fifty-seven million, then ninety-two million dollars.
In November 2013, Balwani told Holmes the company was down to fifteen million dollars in cash.

visual.header: Trial evidence, per the Ninth Circuit
visual.title: Balwani to Holmes · Nov 2013

scenes.say: Yet at Holmes's trial, one investor testified she was shown a projected profit of two hundred and thirty million dollars by the end of 2015.

visual.title: Told vs reported
items: total income reported to the IRS for 2015

scenes.say: Investors were also led to believe the military used the device. At Holmes's trial, General James Mattis testified it was never fielded.
And reports carried the logos of drug companies that, their representatives said, had never validated the technology or allowed their logos to be used.

visual.header: Trial evidence, per the Ninth Circuit
visual.title: Validation reports

scenes.say: In the court's words, Holmes and Balwani painted a very different picture to investors.

visual.text: Holmes and Balwani painted a very different picture to investors.

scenes.say: Prosecutors say Balwani reviewed and approved a 2013 Wall Street Journal article calling the technology faster, cheaper and more accurate. They called that false and misleading.
They also say the pair claimed Walgreens wellness centres would grow from a few dozen to nine hundred, while knowing the relationship was stagnating.
The Securities and Exchange Commission also charged Balwani in 2018. Those are allegations; he chose to fight them in court.

visual.title: Press release 2018-41
lines: !SEC will litigate its claims against Balwani

scenes.say: Chapter five. Two trials. Same judge, same company. So why different verdicts?
Holmes and Balwani were tried separately, both before Judge Edward Davila. The trials were split after Holmes accused him of abuse in their relationship, which he denied.
In January 2022, Holmes's jury convicted her on four investor counts, acquitted her on all four patient charges, and hung on three more.
One clear difference: Holmes took the stand. Balwani did not.
His lawyer reminded jurors that silence was his constitutional right.

visual.text: That is his constitutional right, and it cannot be used in any way against him.
visual.by: Jeffrey Coopersmith, Balwani's lawyer, via CNN

scenes.say: The government called about two dozen witnesses: patients, investors, former employees and business partners. The defence called two.
ABC's Rebecca Jarvis called it the biggest difference between the trials.

visual.text: The biggest difference is that he didn't take the stand to say, 'I didn't do this.'

scenes.say: His defence leaned on missing evidence: a database of test results that no longer existed. In a scientific fraud case, his lawyer argued, you need the scientific data.

visual.title: The missing database
lines: !...you need to have the scientific data."

scenes.say: The prosecutor called that speculation, and told jurors Balwani was no victim.

visual.text: Mr. Balwani is not a victim, he is the perpetrator of the fraud.

scenes.say: Closing arguments alone took nearly four days.

visual.text: Closing arguments last nearly four days

scenes.say: On the seventh of July 2022, after a four-month trial, the jury convicted him on all twelve counts, investors and patients alike.

visual.title: United States v. Balwani
lines: Two conspiracy counts, ten wire fraud counts

scenes.say: A verdict gives no reasons, so we won't guess what either jury thought.

scenes.say: In December, Judge Davila sentenced him to a hundred and fifty-five months. Twelve years and eleven months, longer than Holmes.
In May 2023, the court ordered the two of them, jointly, to repay four hundred and fifty-two million dollars.

visual.label: restitution, owed jointly by Holmes and Balwani
visual.src: 9th Cir. amended opinion, 22 Dec 2025; AP via WYPR, 17 May 2023

scenes.src: 9th Cir. amended opinion, 22 Dec 2025; AP via WYPR, 17 May 2023

scenes.say: Prosecutors had asked for about eight hundred million. Both defendants, AP reported, said they were nearly broke after their legal bills.
Chapter six. The false testimony. If a witness got it wrong, why didn't that matter?
An investor witness, Bryan Tolbert, testified that Holmes said Theranos devices were used on military medevac helicopters.

visual.header: Trial testimony, per the Ninth Circuit
visual.title: Witness: Bryan Tolbert

scenes.say: The appeals court accepted that statement was actually false. On that point, it said, Balwani is technically correct.
Prosecutors have a duty not to let false testimony stand. The court assumed, without deciding, that the duty applied here.

visual.text: We assume without deciding that the government had a duty to correct the inaccurate statement.

scenes.say: Here's the sentence we promised. Because he didn't raise this objection at trial, the court reviewed it only for plain error, and found it did not seriously affect his rights.

visual.title: Why the conviction stood
items: He didn't use the recording to challenge Tolbert
visual.src: 9th Cir. amended opinion, 22 Dec 2025; Balwani cert. petition, 21 May 2026

scenes.src: 9th Cir. amended opinion, 22 Dec 2025; Balwani cert. petition, 21 May 2026

scenes.say: At least two other witnesses, the court said, gave similar testimony. And Balwani never used the recording of the 2013 call to challenge Tolbert.

visual.title: The court's reasons
items: times the call recording was used to impeach

scenes.say: The court also found some lab directors gave expert opinions without being qualified as experts. Harmless, it said. They would have qualified anyway.
In December 2025, it refused to rehear the case. No judge asked for a full-court vote.
His lawyers took both points to the Supreme Court. The government waived its right to respond.

visual.header: Supreme Court of the United States
visual.title: Balwani v. United States

scenes.say: On the fifth of October 2026, the petition was denied, without a word of explanation.
Our analysis. So why did the case against the number two hold where the case against the founder partly failed?
This is our reading, not the court's. The patient case was about a lab, and the court record puts Balwani in charge of that lab.

visual.title: Our reading
items: The patient case was about the lab
The court says Balwani oversaw it
The regulator's letter named him as owner

scenes.src: 9th Cir. amended opinion, 22 Dec 2025; CMS letter to Theranos, 18 Mar 2016

scenes.say: Holmes told her side for days. Balwani's jury heard no answer from him.
And the false testimony? The courts didn't say it was harmless to tell it. They said it didn't change the outcome, given everything else.

visual.text: Did not seriously affect his substantial rights.

scenes.say: Who paid? Investors, who were owed three hundred and ninety-seven million dollars of the restitution. Walgreens and Safeway. And patients who were handed numbers they trusted about their own bodies.
